lines.say: Year elevens, your revision timetable doesn't fail because you're lazy. It fails because paper can't move.
One evening goes wrong, the whole week's out of date, and on Sunday you start again.
And cramming it all back in on Sunday doesn't work either. Spreading revision out beats cramming. It's called spacing, and the research on it goes back over a century.
Offload works differently. Download your spec from your exam board, upload it with your exam dates, and it builds the plan from that.
Miss an evening, and it moves the work into your free time, and tells you what moved.
Offload. A study system that adapts when real life happens.
